correctness.rationale: A positive-probability block of spanning row projectors is strictly contracting: norm equality would fix a vector orthogonal to the spanning rows. Independent blocks give exponential L^r decay for their products and almost sure contraction, so the Gaussian pullback converges in every finite L^r and shared-drive coupling gives uniqueness even without assuming moments of a rival invariant law. For an initial law of only finite fourth moment, use the moment-coupling statement only through r=4. Stationary mean is zero by positive definiteness of Σp_i u_i u_i^T. A centered Gaussian stationarity mixture can agree with a single Gaussian only when all component covariances agree, by variance of the directional variances. The equation S_i=S is equivalent to Su_i=s_i u_i; hence equal eigenvalues on each nonorthogonality edge are necessary and the orthogonal component covariance is sufficient. The conditional covariance Γ of the pullback gives 3 Var(v^TΓv), and conditioning on the last row proves the bound. Incompatibility makes at least one S_i−S nonzero, so some direction's bound is already strictly positive, not necessarily every direction's. Independent exact replay: python /workspace/audit_checks/kaczmarz_conditional_variances.py. It solves the conditional scalar variance process in dimension two and reproduced all three reported rationals (covariance, fourth cumulant and lower bound); it checks that example only. The uploaded program was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: A necessary and sufficient graph test for invariant Gaussianity works for arbitrary spanning row families, including overdetermined ones, irrespective of the positive sampling law.
